Subject: Request: carve-out for confidentiality/trade-secrets + evidence preservation

Priya / Redwood team —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As discussed on the call, our legal team needs to carve out breaches involving trade secrets/confidential patient data from Redwood's liability cap and to define an evidence-preservation protocol that lets Aegis assess forensic damage.

High level asks from Aegis Legal:
- A narrow carve-out to the liability cap for proven confidentiality breaches that expose trade secrets or PHI; we may seek uncapped damages in those narrow circumstances.
- A formal written evidence-preservation plan (what Redwood will preserve and for how long) covering API request logs, model input/output artifacts, KV-cache snapshots where feasible, and admin access records.
- Clear SLAs for preservation after notice (we expect the ability to request artifacts within a fixed window).

Please share Redwood's proposed redline language for the MSA/order form and an operations-level checklist we can provide to our internal security team. Also confirm whether Redwood will permit third-party forensic review (under NDA) and what logs/artifacts are realistically collectable.

We need to move quickly — our procurement team wants to finalize legal redlines by EOW. Happy to set a short call tomorrow.

Best,
Elena Soto

Subject: Proposed redline + evidence-preservation protocol (draft)

Elena / team —

Attached is our proposed redline and a short evidence-preservation protocol (see Attachment: Aegis-Evidence-Protocol-v1.docx). Key points of the legal drafting (summary):

- Scope: The carve-out is limited to breaches that (i) materially expose Aegis trade secrets or regulated PHI and (ii) are the proximate result of Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with its service obligations. We rejected an unconditional uncapped exposure to keep the carve-out narrowly focused.
- Trigger: Aegis provides written notice describing the suspected incident; Redwood will preserve the requested artifacts for a 90-day preservation period while parties investigate.
- Forensic access: Subject to an NDA and mutually agreed scope, Redwood will provide (for the specific sessions/keys identified): API request/response logs, model input/output snapshots, system-level admin logs, and any persisted artifacts related to the affected tenant. KV cache snapshots are technically limited — see Jonas’ note below — and will be produced only where they can be isolated to the incident and where doing so does not compromise other tenants.
- Mitigation & dispute: Redwood must be given a reasonable opportunity to remediate (14 days) before uncapped damages are pursued, except where immediate preservation is needed to prevent spoliation.

Please review the proposed clause in the redline PDF. Specific questions for Aegis:
- Is 90 days preservation acceptable, or do you require a longer window?
- Are you comfortable with the notice + remediation window model?
- Will Aegis accept a scoped third-party forensics process under a narrow NDA?

If we can agree on these points, we can fold the redline into the order form and move to signature.

Regards,

Team / Elena —

Quick technical notes to make the preservation plan actionable:

- Logs & metadata: We retain detailed request/response logs (timestamps, request headers, routing) by default for 30 days. We can extend retention to 90 days for a customer-specific contract (there is an associated storage+support cost).
- Model I/O snapshots: We can persist generated outputs and model inputs for specific request IDs if those IDs are provided in the preservation notice. We do not, as a matter of platform design, persist every ephemeral internal state by default.
- KV cache: The runtime KV cache is an in-memory optimization. Snapshots are only possible when a request is pinned to a session we can reproduce from request IDs and model state; otherwise a full cache dump is not feasible without impacting multi-tenant isolation. For incidents where a reproducible session exists, we can extract a limited KV snapshot for that session and scrub tenant identifiers where applicable.
- Embeddings/indexes: If Aegis is using hosted embeddings or a Redwood-managed index, we can export vectors tied to the tenant with a signed request. Export takes ~2–3 business days once authorized.

Operational asks from Redwood: a) a formal preservation notice with request IDs (or approximate time ranges), b) agreement on paid retention if >30 days, and c) authorization for a narrow forensics engagement (NDA + scope).

Happy to walk through examples on the call.

— Jonas
Head of Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
